sections.html:
• Scientific name: Aspidoras depinnai Britto, 2000
  • Common names: Ipojuca Catfish; Ipojuca-pansermalle (Denmark)
  • Type locality: Creek at Amaraji-Primavera road, rio Ipojuca basin, 8°21'S, 35°26'W, Pernambuco State, Brazil.
  • Etymology: Aspidoras: from the Greek aspis, meaning shield, and doras, meaning skin; in reference to the bony plates. Named to honour Dr. Mário de Pinna.
  • IUCN Red List: Least Concern (last assessed 2018).
South America: Ipojuca River basin, Brazil. Southern Atlantic Draining Rivers, North East Brazil Coastal Rivers, Pernambucu state waters, Ipojuca.

Ideally substrate should be sand, but rounded gravel is an imperfect alternative. Avoid keeping over rough edged (chipped) gravel, as this will increase the risk of damage to the fish's barbels when it tries to dig. Substrate should be bordered with driftwood and aquatic plants, leaving an open area for them to search for food and swim. The shade provided by overhanging rock work, arching bogwood, tall or floating plants is all that is required to settle these fishes.

Will readily accept all prepared foods that reach the bottom of the aquarium such as tablets, granules and larger flakes. Live (or frozen) foods such as bloodworm, white worm, grindal worm (Enchytraeus), Daphnia and Tubifex are readily accepted and good for conditioning groups of fishes for spawning.
Females grow larger and are more full-bodied, this is best observed from above the fish. Males will typically have more pointed as opposed to more rounded fin tips as they mature.

Spawning notes kindly provided by Eric Bodrock from August 2007. A group consisting of five males and three females (all F1) were spawned in a ten-gallon tank (40 litres), pH of 6.8 with an average temperature around 24°C. The dGH 8 with a KH of 2. Regular spawning took place about every 3 weeks, on average about 60 eggs, usually deposited on glass sides and/or in the bottom spawning mop. The hatch rate was always low; it is estimated to take about one year for them to reach sexual maturity.
